definitions.explanation: The fundamental starting point or basis of something. Used figuratively to refer to the core principles or beginnings that define a person, project, or idea. Also used in mathematics and coordinates to mean the origin point (0,0).

examples.japanese: {原点|げんてん}に{立|た}ち{返|かえ}る。
examples.english: To go back to the starting point.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}したときは{原点|げんてん}に{戻|もど}って{考|かんが}え{直|なお}すべきだ。
examples.english: When you fail, you should return to the basics and reconsider.

examples.japanese: この{場所|ばしょ}が{彼|かれ}の{音楽家|おんがくか}としての{原点|げんてん}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This place is said to be his starting point as a musician.

notes:
Often used metaphorically to express the idea of returning to fundamentals or rediscovering one's roots. The phrase {原点|げんてん}に{立|た}ち{返|かえ}る or {原点|げんてん}に{戻|もど}る (to return to the origin) is extremely common.

Not to be confused with {減点|げんてん} (deduction of points), which is a homophone with a completely different meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{原点|げんてん}に{戻|もど}る — to return to the starting point
・{原点|げんてん}に{立|た}ち{返|かえ}る — to go back to basics
・{原点|げんてん}{回帰|かいき} — returning to one's roots
・{創業|そうぎょう}の{原点|げんてん} — founding origins
